Any coercion, inserted default/generated ID/time, v1 migration, CaseInput label/confidence normalization, or ToolResult normalization therefore returns artifact_schema_error; these and unknown fields, string-to-number, bool/int, container, and datetime coercions are adversarial cases. state.json, .poker-deliberation-run, every unlisted logical name/media/schema combination, and opaque-bytes-v1 are refused in P2-012A.

Classification admission and replay: RevisionArtifact must contain the complete ArtifactClassification and trusted evidence inputs, typed origin_kind, and declared policy SHA-256. Before lock/filesystem mutation the store reruns classify_artifact(logical_name, every exact ClassificationEvidence field), requires exact classification, classification_source, and P2-027A policy SHA-256 508fe62ce72ae54b59a8d71e200309a2046bf807dcf249f0aebf787c910cab60, refuses ClassificationSource.DEFAULT_INTERNAL, and requires trusted explicit or verified source-inherited public/internal classification with a completed clean restricted-secret check for both. The complete non-secret evidence, source, derived evidence hash, and policy binding are persisted; every structural read/reachable-history/orphan verification strictly reconstructs ArtifactClassification, reruns the same classifier under that exact policy, and requires equality with inventory and LocalDataBindingV1. Attempt context, sensitive, restricted, unknown, downgrade, mismatch, forged evidence hash, or encryption-required data is denied. This replayable provenance is structural verification only and grants no P2-012B lifecycle action.

Context boundary: ContextPolicy and ContextEnvelope stay schema 1.0.0 with poker-context-json-v1 and attempt-memory-only-v1. Raw ContextEnvelope, canonical provider context payload, ContextPolicy, credentials, and blinded upstream provider/agent input are never payload artifacts; only non-secret typed context hashes/lineage may appear in provenance. CaseInput, normalized artifacts, and final synthesis may contain the already-approved full retrospective hand/result information under their existing schemas and blind-isolation flow. Storage does not act as a semantic blind-isolation detector and does not claim to detect every secret or defeat a malicious trusted caller that forges classification evidence.

Typed provenance union: the only binding kind literals are approval_decision, context, phase, budget_policy, tool, local_data, source, and report; every binding has that discriminator and only immutable scalar/tuple kind-specific fields, whose hashes retain their originating framework domains rather than being reinterpreted by storage canonicalization. ApprovalDecisionBindingV1 contains kind, approval_id, decision restricted to approved or rejected, decided_at, decision_reason_sha256, and external_source_id. decision_reason_sha256 is SHA-256 of ASCII poker-approval-decision-reason-v1, one 0x00 byte, and the exact NFC UTF-8 decision_reason. external_source_id is exactly approval-decision- plus approval_id. Its canonical decision evidence projection contains only approval_id, status, decision_reason, and decided_at in the approved storage UTC form; source_sha256 is SHA-256 of ASCII poker-approval-decision-evidence-v1, one 0x00 byte, and canonical JSON of that projection. The binding records correlation only and does not validate actor identity, authority, or decision CAS, which remain P2-013. ContextBindingV1 contains kind, context_sha256, context_id, attempt_id, nullable parent_context_id, schema_version, classification, payload_sha256, source_sha256, policy_sha256, envelope_sha256, expires_at UTC, producer_runtime, and consumer_runtime and cross-checks every corresponding AgentExecutionRecord field. PhaseBindingV1 contains kind, run_id, phase_id, phase_schema_version, attempt_id, ordered unique context_ids, input_hash, policy_snapshot_hash, nullable output_hash, and the exact ordered ArtifactIntent tuple of kind, relative_path, media_type, and nullable content_sha256 from the bound PhaseOutcome. Every tuple field/null is preserved and cross-checked; the current synthesis state.json intent remains in PhaseBinding evidence but is excluded from P2-012A payload admission, intents grant no write authority, and each admitted intent with nonnull content_sha256 must match its inventory entry. BudgetPolicyBindingV1 contains kind, policy_schema_version fixed to the exact BudgetPolicyV2.schema_version value, and policy_sha256 only; no nonexistent policy_version field is invented. ToolBindingV1 contains kind, run_id, phase_attempt_id, ordinal, request_id, request_tool_name, requested_by, requires_approval, nullable requested_contract_version, tool_request_sha256, request_input_artifact_sha256, result_id, result_tool_name, result_artifact_sha256, request_input_sha256, validated_result_input_sha256, materialized_result_input_sha256, supported_contract_version, and result_contract_version. Every copied nonnull version string, including phase_schema_version, context schema_version, report_schema_version, and tool contract versions, must match ^[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z._+-]{0,63}$ and its originating typed value exactly. tool_request_sha256 is phases.contracts.canonical_sha256 over the complete ToolRequest request_id/tool_name/input/requested_by/requires_approval/contract_version projection; preflight reconstructs and strictly revalidates that complete request from immutable fields plus the paired input artifact, revalidates the exact result artifact, and enforces every current ToolExecutionBinding correlation. LocalDataBindingV1 contains kind, policy_id, policy_version, policy_sha256, logical_name, classification, classification_source, complete classification_evidence, and derived classification_evidence_sha256; every artifact has exactly one and it must equal every corresponding RevisionArtifactV1 and inventory field. SourceBindingV1 contains kind, source_id, source_kind restricted to user_input, payload_artifact, or external_evidence, trust_kind restricted respectively to trusted_user_input, verified_payload, or declared_external_evidence, nullable source_logical_name, nullable source_schema_version, nullable consumer_record_id, and source_sha256. user_input/external_evidence require null source_schema_version; payload_artifact requires exact equality with the referenced inventory artifact_schema_version. ReportBindingV1 contains kind, report_id, report_schema_version, report_json_sha256, rendered_markdown_sha256, and upstream_source_sha256; for final_report.md, report_id equals FinalReport.run_id, report_schema_version equals final_report.json artifact_schema_version, report_json_sha256 equals that inventory payload hash, rendered_markdown_sha256 equals the markdown payload hash, and upstream_source_sha256 equals final_report.json inventory source_sha256.

Immutable snapshot boundary: RevisionArtifactV1 construction immediately deep model-dumps and revalidates any existing domain model, classification evidence, and provenance input, canonicalizes them into owned immutable bytes plus scalar/tuple storage bindings, and discards all caller-owned dict/list/model references. RevisionPublishRequestV1 likewise owns a tuple of those snapshots; pure preflight and locked publication read only owned bytes/snapshots and never reread caller objects. Caller-owned mutable inputs must not be mutated from constructor entry until snapshot success; detected structural mutation is rejected, but undetectable concurrent same-shape value mutation during construction is outside the supported threat model. After successful snapshot creation, any original-object mutation before or during publish cannot change transaction, inventory, manifest, or stored bytes and is covered by adversarial tests.

Provenance order and digest: binding_sha256 is a derived nonserialized value equal to SHA-256 of ASCII poker-run-provenance-binding-v1, one 0x00 byte, and the complete canonical binding JSON, so no binding self-reference exists. The total order is the typed tuple of kind UTF-8 bytes followed by the kind-specific primary identity: approval request ID, context_id/attempt_id, run_id/phase_id/attempt_id, budget policy SHA-256, run_id/phase_attempt_id/ordinal as a nonnegative integer/result_id, policy ID/logical_name, source ID, or report ID; canonical binding bytes break any remaining tie. Exact duplicate binding digests and duplicate primary identity with different bytes are rejected. Manifest provenance_heads are ordered by kind UTF-8 bytes and each head is SHA-256 of ASCII poker-run-provenance-head-v1, one 0x00 byte, kind UTF-8, one 0x00 byte, and canonical JSON of that kind's ordered binding digests.

Provenance correlation and exact source graph: every artifact has exactly one LocalDataBindingV1. Its policy_id is exactly p2-027a-local-data-policy-v1, policy_version exactly 1.0.0, and policy_sha256 equals RevisionArtifactV1.policy_sha256 and the fixed approved digest; its logical name, classification, classification source/evidence/hash exactly equal the RevisionArtifact and inventory fields, while inventory deliberately does not duplicate policy fields. Every payload_artifact SourceBinding must name an earlier artifact in the approved current-orchestrator dependency order and must exactly match that same-revision inventory entry's logical_name, artifact_schema_version, and payload SHA-256; source_id is payload- plus SHA-256 of ASCII poker-payload-source-id-v1, one 0x00 byte, and source logical-name UTF-8; trust_kind=verified_payload and consumer_record_id=null. Self, future, circular, cross-run, duplicate, conflicting, or unlisted payload edges fail closed. input.json has exactly one user_input SourceBinding with source_id=user-input, trust_kind=trusted_user_input, null logical/schema/consumer fields, and source_sha256 equal to SHA-256 of ASCII poker-user-input-source-v1, one 0x00 byte, and exact input payload bytes. normalized_case.json, assumptions.json, and security_events.json each bind input.json. approvals.json binds input.json; every pending ApprovalRequest has no ApprovalDecisionBinding, while every approved/rejected request requires exactly one matching ApprovalDecisionBindingV1 and exactly one external_evidence SourceBinding with source_id equal to external_source_id, trust_kind=declared_external_evidence, null logical/schema/consumer fields, and source_sha256 equal to the canonical decision-evidence hash; status, nonnull reason/decided_at, reason hash, and evidence projection must match the strict ApprovalRequest. Storage does not claim actor authority or approval CAS. evidence.jsonl has one external_evidence SourceBinding per strict EvidenceRecord: source_id and consumer_record_id both equal evidence_id, trust_kind=declared_external_evidence, logical/schema null, and source_sha256 is SHA-256 of ASCII poker-evidence-record-source-v1, one 0x00 byte, and canonical JSON of that complete record; it also has one file-level payload binding to input.json. assignments.json binds normalized_case.json. agent_execution_records.json binds assignments.json and normalized_case.json plus matching ContextBindingV1 and PhaseBindingV1. Each agent_reports/*.json binds assignments.json and normalized_case.json plus matching ContextBindingV1 and PhaseBindingV1; if the ordered unique union of AgentReport.evidence_ids and every nested Claim.evidence_ids is nonempty it also binds evidence.jsonl exactly once and every declared ID must resolve to a strict record in that file, and it binds each distinct earlier tool_results/<id>.json named by the ordered unique AgentReport.tool_result_ids. Duplicate, unknown, cross-run, or future evidence/tool IDs fail closed; the later aggregate execution ledger is correlation evidence, not a report data source. Each tool_results/*.input.json binds input.json and normalized_case.json, never assignments.json, plus matching PhaseBindingV1 and ToolBindingV1; its paired tool_results/*.json binds exactly that input artifact plus matching PhaseBindingV1 and ToolBindingV1. disputes.json binds every present agent report and tool-result JSON, never tool-input alone. final_report.json binds input.json, normalized_case.json, assumptions.json, evidence.jsonl exactly once, approvals.json, assignments.json, agent_execution_records.json, security_events.json, every agent report, every tool input/result pair, and disputes.json plus declared context/phase heads and BudgetPolicyBindingV1. Its embedded evidence, approvals, agent_execution_records, security_events, tool_results, and disputes arrays must equal the corresponding parsed ledger payloads exactly in order and content. final_report.md has exactly one payload_artifact SourceBinding naming final_report.json and exactly one fully correlated ReportBindingV1. source_sha256 is SHA-256 of ASCII poker-run-upstream-bindings-v1, one 0x00 byte, and canonical JSON of direct SourceBindingV1 values sorted first by the typed logical-name key (0, empty bytes) for null or (1, source_logical_name UTF-8) otherwise, then source_id UTF-8, then by (0, empty bytes) for null consumer_record_id or (1, consumer_record_id UTF-8) otherwise; null therefore sorts before nonnull without coercion. Property tests permute user_input, external_evidence, and payload_artifact bindings including null/non-null fields and reject every trust mismatch, record mismatch, duplicate, and future-edge permutation.

Control metadata safety: producer_id and producer_version are injected trusted application constants, not caller free text. Every caller-originated control/provenance identifier uses its existing strict typed ID or the tested portable grammar with the existing 128-character bound; versions use a fixed approved literal or the existing bounded contract-version field. All control strings require NFC, reject path/URI/control characters and Windows reserved aliases where path-like, and pass the P2-027A secret-metadata detector before serialization; raw absolute paths, arbitrary messages, credentials, payload excerpts, and unbounded free text are forbidden in manifests, transactions, pointers, lock metadata, recovery claims, outcomes, and provenance.

Layout: root-init authority=<revision_root>/.revision-init.authority.lock; ownership marker=<revision_root>/ownership.json and temp=<revision_root>/ownership.<root_id>.tmp; initialization directory temps=<revision_root>/.revision-control.<root_id>.tmp and <revision_root>/runs.<root_id>.tmp; run authority=<revision_root>/.revision-control/locks/<run_id_sha256>.authority.lock; metadata=<revision_root>/.revision-control/locks/<run_id_sha256>.metadata.json; metadata temp=<revision_root>/.revision-control/locks/<run_id_sha256>.<owner_token>.metadata.tmp; namespace parents=<revision_root>/runs/<run_id>/.revision-store plus transactions, revisions, recovery-claims, and recovery-claims/.tmp; current=<revision_root>/runs/<run_id>/.revision-store/current.json; pointer temp=<revision_root>/runs/<run_id>/.revision-store/current.<transaction_id>.tmp; staging=<revision_root>/runs/<run_id>/.revision-store/transactions/<transaction_id>/ containing transaction.json, payload/<logical_name>, and manifest.json; immutable revision=<revision_root>/runs/<run_id>/.revision-store/revisions/r<revision>-<transaction_id>/ containing the same transaction.json, payload, and manifest; claim temp=<revision_root>/runs/<run_id>/.revision-store/recovery-claims/.tmp/<transaction_id>.<claim_id>.json; claim final=<revision_root>/runs/<run_id>/.revision-store/recovery-claims/<transaction_id>.json.

Preflight and quota order: pure preflight performs all request/schema/path/classification/media/canonical/provenance checks, exact payload/control sizes, per-artifact limits, and proposed-byte planning before any filesystem mutation. Authority bootstrap/acquisition may then create or repair only the fixed control byte. Under the lock, a mandatory existing-namespace scan first validates bound legacy identity, root/run identity, known entry grammar, regular/link/reparse rules, current/reachable lineage, and current physical total against max_run_bytes; unknown/link/over-cap state fails closed even for replay. Idempotency/current/CAS is then evaluated, and a valid idempotent or conflicting request returns without metadata or namespace write. A genuinely new publish next admits its exact coexistence peak before metadata, namespace bootstrap, staging, claim, or current mutation. Equality is allowed; one byte over fails. A first-use quota/CAS/idempotency refusal can report filesystem_effect=control_only from authority bootstrap but always reports current unchanged.

Byte limits: reuse tested defaults max_artifact_bytes=1000000 and max_run_bytes=10000000; accept only strict positive integers and reject bool/coercion/nonpositive overrides. Per-artifact applies to each payload and canonical control file. Per-run includes current plus temp coexistence, all reachable revisions, staging, unreferenced revisions, claim final/temp files, metadata final/temp, and the attributable one-byte run authority file. Empty approved namespace directories consume no counted file bytes but remain structurally verified. Unknown, link/reparse, hardlinked, or non-regular entries fail closed. Filesystem allocation units, compression, snapshots, root-global ownership/root-init-authority bytes, and flat-v1 files are outside the claim.

Publish order: preflight; process-local nonblocking lock; stable one-byte kernel lock; mandatory locked existing-namespace/identity/link/known-entry/current-lineage/current-byte-cap scan; idempotency and current/CAS read with early return for replay/conflict; exact coexistence-peak admission for a new publish; advisory metadata replace; explicit namespace bootstrap creating each approved run/.revision-store/transactions/revisions/recovery-claims/.tmp parent one level at a time with identity reread; unique staging and transaction descriptor; each payload exclusive write/flush/close/reread/verify; manifest write/flush/close/reread/full inventory verify; same-filesystem staging-to-revision rename; immutable revision plus verified-lineage reread; pointer-temp write/flush/close/reread; root/legacy identity and expected-current recheck; atomic current replace; current/manifest/inventory/lineage reconciliation; supported directory-sync attempts; lock release. Existing exact empty approved namespace parents are idempotently reusable; any unknown/nonempty unexpected/link/identity-mismatched parent fails closed.

CAS and idempotency: compare expected_revision, expected_manifest_sha256, and expected_pointer_sha256 under the lock both before staging and before replace. Same transaction plus same transaction digest at current returns current_committed; if present in verified reachable history returns historical_committed with observed current; if only staging or unreachable revision exists returns reconciliation_required; same transaction plus different digest is idempotency_conflict; stale expected state after lock acquisition is run_conflict. No case silently republishes, advances current, or chooses highest revision.

Reachability: the structural reader starts at a strictly verified current pointer and follows each manifest previous_revision and previous_manifest_sha256 to revision 1/null while enforcing exact decrement, run identity, unique transaction/revision path, transaction descriptor digest, full inventory, and immutable byte hashes. reachable_history is that complete verified chain. Missing/tampered/cyclic/cross-run lineage is corrupt; no partial chain is called verified. Only staging or published revisions outside reachable_history are orphans.

Lock contract: an in-process nonreentrant registry keyed by pinned canonical root identity plus ownership-marker SHA-256 plus ASCII-case-folded run ID prevents same-process instances/threads and root aliases from bypassing process-scoped OS locks. Registry reserve is the first lock action, kernel acquire follows, and release occurs in finally after kernel release attempt; a release fault keeps the registry entry conservatively held for that store process and returns effect_unknown rather than allowing reentry. The stable authority file contains exactly one constant byte; bootstrap or zero-length crash repair writes that byte in place, verifies identity/hardlink count, and never replaces, unlinks, or truncates it. The Windows adapter uses binary mode, seek(0), and msvcrt LK_NBLCK for exactly byte range offset 0 length 1; the POSIX adapter uses fcntl.flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB on the whole authority file and makes no byte-range claim. Metadata is advisory last-owner data, never authority, is atomically replaced under lock, and is not deleted at release. Every acquisition uses its fresh owner_token in the exclusive metadata-temp path; a partial prior temp is a recognized quota-counted control orphan that never blocks a later acquisition's fresh temp, and corrupt/stale final metadata may be replaced only after lock acquisition.

Platform interpretation of the immutable milestone lock criterion: the canonical acceptance text about a one-byte file locked at offset zero for length one is implemented literally by the Windows msvcrt adapter. On POSIX, flock has whole-file semantics; because the verified authority file contains exactly one byte, the whole-file lock excludes all access to that one-byte authority but is not represented or claimed as a POSIX byte-range lock. Platform-specific tests assert these distinct APIs without changing the immutable milestone text.

Wait/stale/retry policy: acquisition makes one nonblocking attempt with no timeout, bounded wait, lease, heartbeat, monotonic stale threshold, cancellation, lock stealing, or automatic retry. PID and UTC are audit-only. RunLocked has retryable=true but automatic_retry_allowed=false; filesystem_effect is none if this call did not bootstrap/repair and control_only if it did before losing the kernel race, while domain/current remain unchanged. All other failures have retryable=false. An overlap returns RunLocked; a separately invoked writer after winner release may acquire and then return RunConflict for stale expected state.

Read and inspect mutation rule: ordinary current/revision structural reads never acquire or create a lock and use pointer-read, full verify, pointer-reread consistency. inspect_orphans requires an already-existing valid one-byte authority and acquires process/kernel locks without creating/repairing authority or writing metadata; missing, zero-length, corrupt, linked, or identity-mismatched authority returns lock_unavailable with mutation zero. Recovery claim is a separate mutating operation and may update metadata/claim files under its locked admission.

Recovery claim: inspect and claim require the authoritative lock and verify the target is staging or an unreferenced published revision outside reachable_history. Only descriptor_verified or manifest_verified targets with a verified transaction_sha256 are claimable; path_only/partial staging is reported by inspection but claim returns run_incomplete with mutation zero. Claim binds transaction ID/digest, observed pointer SHA-256, orphan form, request-stable claimant token, and strict injected UTC. A claim-specific temp is exclusive-created, canonical-written, flushed, reread, and atomically finalized under lock only after final absence and reachability recheck; existing exact valid claim is idempotent across a new process/new lock owner, different valid is recovery_claim_conflict, invalid final is recovery_claim_incomplete with reconciliation required, and partial temp is a recognized quota-counted orphan. Finalize-success followed by result/reconcile fault and a new-process retry of the same request must return the exact idempotent claim. Claim alone grants no publish/approval authority and performs no move/delete/repair/quarantine/adoption.

Path/threat contract: resolve and pin the dedicated root, reject root or descendant symlink/junction/reparse using Python-3.11-compatible lstat and Windows FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT checks, require regular files with link count one, exclusive-create mutable temps, and recheck canonical identity at every deterministic write/publish/CAS boundary. Logical paths reject empty/dot/dot-dot, absolute, drive-relative/absolute, UNC, device, URI, slash mismatch, backslash, colon/ADS, reserved stem, trailing dot/space, NFC alias, and ASCII-case alias. Detected effects reflect the stage; complete syscall-between malicious same-privilege TOCTOU, authenticity, ACL hardening, and native-handle sandboxing are not claimed.

Path-length capability: each operation's pure preflight constructs every concrete path it can use before that operation's first mutation. acceptance_criteria: P2-010B implements only an internal, explicit, revision-only synthesis commit seam. It does not connect ordinary Orchestrator.run, resume, load_report, CLI run/resume/show, AppConfig.runs_dir, or an existing flat-v1 run ID to revision storage, because P2-012A rejects legacy/revision namespace overlap and P2-012B owns product integration.

The integration revalidates the exact P2-010A schema-1.0.0 Synthesis PhaseRequest and PhaseOutcome correlation for run_id, phase_id, attempt_id, context_ids, input_hash, policy_snapshot_hash, output_hash, status, requested_next_state, and artifact intents before any revision-store call; only a succeeded synthesis outcome requesting completed is admitted.

The orchestrator prepares phase-transition-plan-v1 while the machine is in FINAL_SYNTHESIS without mutation. Its frozen canonical JSON data fields are exactly schema_version 1.0.0, run_id, source FINAL_SYNTHESIS, target COMPLETED, literal reason durable synthesis revision committed, event_count, event_prefix_sha256, and plan_sha256. The prefix digest is SHA-256 over the domain bytes poker-phase-transition-event-prefix-v1 followed by one zero byte and compact ensure_ascii=false/sort_keys=true/allow_nan=false JSON for the ordered source/target/reason event list. plan_sha256 is SHA-256 over the analogous poker-phase-transition-plan-v1 zero-byte domain followed by the compact canonical JSON of exactly the preceding seven data fields, excluding plan_sha256. Illegal, stale, non-factory-issued, divergent, wrong-reason, wrong-version, or non-synthesis plans fail closed before publication.

The coordinator binds each admitted non-state artifact intent to an exact canonical payload byte sequence and lowercase SHA-256. A null outcome content hash is deterministically filled in the persisted PhaseBindingV1 snapshot from those admitted bytes; a nonnull hash must already match. The state.json intent remains represented but is not materialized because P2-012A is structural_nonterminal and P2-012B owns durable state checkpoints.

The proposed revision contains the complete P2-012A-admitted source graph needed for the synthesis artifacts and exact typed provenance. PhaseBindingV1, ContextBindingV1, ToolBindingV1, BudgetPolicyBindingV1, SourceBindingV1, approval, report, assignment, tool, run, attempt, policy, and context correlations must replay successfully under the separately approved poker-final-report-artifact-v2 contract. P2-010B itself changes no storage canonical/model/store code or version: final report v1 remains lexical-order plus mandatory-context, while v2 validates one identical input/result binding per execution, unique contiguous projected ordinals, ordinal report order, and exactly zero context only for a trace with no agent reports and no execution records.

The internal frozen phase trace includes the exact Synthesis request/outcome, every contributing ContextBuild request/outcome, every Analysis request/outcome, and every ToolResearch request/outcome with complete ToolExecutionBinding values. The coordinator revalidates phase hashes and correlations, ContextDispatch and envelope integrity/assignment/allowlist/attempt-memory-only policy at the recorded creation boundary, validate_analysis_output, and validate_tool_research_output, derives the persisted PhaseBindingV1 and ContextBindingV1 values from those preimages, and rejects missing, extra, duplicate, self-consistent-hash-only, or cross-trace provenance. Raw ContextEnvelope, ContextPolicy, AgentContext, dispatch, provider input, and phase-trace preimages stay in memory and are never passed as revision artifacts.

ToolRequest input bytes, ToolResult bytes, requested/supported/result contract versions, request and result IDs, unique contiguous execution ordinals, phase attempt IDs, source/policy hashes, deterministic calculator evidence, seed/sample/iteration/stopping metadata, warnings, errors, and reproduction metadata come from the complete in-memory ToolResearch trace and admitted canonical artifacts. FinalReport.tool_results remains in execution ordinal order even when result IDs have a different UTF-8 lexical order. The integration does not reconstruct a ToolRequest from only ToolResult, rerun a tool or provider effect, reorder or rewrite report bytes, or rewrite numeric evidence.

Before calling RunRevisionStore.publish, the coordinator applies exact-payload-restricted-secret-scan-v1. Each artifact must be no larger than configured RunRevisionStore.max_artifact_bytes and strict UTF-8; JSON scans every recursively parsed object key and string value, JSONL scans every nonempty line the same way, and Markdown scans the whole decoded text. Object keys use case-insensitive substring regex api[-_]?key|authorization|bearer|cookie|password|passwd|secret|token|private[-_]?key|client[-_]?(secret|credential)|credential. Every string value and Markdown text use the exact case-insensitive union regex from P2-027A storage control metadata: \bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b; \bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}\b; \bgithub_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}\b; \b(?:AKIA|ASIA)[A-Z0-9]{16}\b; \bAIza[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}\b; \beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{5,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{5,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{5,}\b; \bxox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}\b; \bnpm_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}\b; \b(?:rk|sk)_(?:live|test)_[A-Za-z0-9]{10,}\b; \bBearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]{8,}\b; and (?:api[-_]?key|password|passwd|secret|token)\s*[:=]. It additionally rejects -----BEGIN (?:RSA |EC |OPENSSH )?PRIVATE KEY----- and case-insensitive \b(?:api[-_]?key|access[-_]?token|password|client[-_]?secret)\b\s*[:=]\s*['\"]?[A-Za-z0-9_./+=-]{12,}. Parse failure, unsupported media/serialization, sensitive/restricted/unknown/downgraded classification, or caller evidence disagreement fails closed.

Every caught coordinator validation, scanner, canonical, and storage Exception is consumed inside a minimal catch boundary and mapped only to a frozen phase-revision-failure-v1 data value with exactly schema_version 1.0.0 and one closed code from invalid_trace, invalid_plan, secret_detected, unsupported_payload, persistence_denied, publish_conflict, publish_uncertain, authorization_mismatch, apply_failed, or apply_unknown. The public coordinator result is a closed success-or-failure data union: phase-revision-failure-v1 is never raised as an exception, contains no exception member, and no caught exception, __cause__, __context__, __traceback__, traceback frame, frame local, raw byte, matched value, ContextEnvelope canonical payload, AgentContext, PhaseRequest/Outcome repr, provider/tool input, or secret crosses or is retained by the seam. The catch boundary emits no raw log or warning and constructs/returns the closed value without embedding or chaining the caught object. Parametrized canaries cover every credential family in innocuous JSON keys, CaseInput.raw_text, nested JSONL, ToolResult, and Markdown with mutation-zero denial; they recursively inspect the returned union, str/repr/log/warning captures, and any exposed object graph to prove that no BaseException, traceback, frame, frame local, canary, or raw payload is reachable.

ContextPolicy and ContextEnvelope remain schema 1.0.0 and attempt-memory-only-v1. Only typed non-secret context identity, classification, source hash, policy hash, lineage, expiry, producer/consumer runtime, envelope hash, and phase input/output hash commitments may persist; provider use-expiry and storage retention remain separate. Provider prompts, ContextEnvelope.canonical_payload, ContextPolicy, AgentContext, dispatch objects, provider payloads, and phase trace preimages are never persisted. A clean approved CaseInput raw_text remains an existing input.json/normalized_case.json field and is not mislabelled as a provider prompt. No secret, retention executor, or lifecycle hook is added.

The transaction_id is the stable idempotency key for the whole canonical RevisionPublishRequestV1. Exact replay must reuse the entire request and digest; same transaction with different bytes fails as idempotency_conflict, stale expected revision fails as run_conflict, overlap fails as run_locked, and P2-010B performs zero automatic retry or wait.

The coordinator returns a frozen nonserializable same-process phase-transition-authorization-v1 only after RunRevisionStore.publish returns published or exact current_committed. Its exact data fields are schema_version 1.0.0, plan, run_id_sha256, transaction_id, transaction_sha256, revision, manifest_sha256, pointer_sha256, and outcome_kind published or current_committed, plus one repr-hidden compare-false private issuer-capability identity that is neither a data field nor persistable. A private factory issues it only from one frozen request/plan bundle after matching the complete outcome run hash, transaction identity/digest, revision, manifest, pointer, closed durability/reconciliation matrix, and confirmed authority release; storage does not contain or attest plan_sha256. Apply requires the exact factory-issued capability identity, exact plan self-hash, exact authorization data, the original in-memory bundle identity, and a fresh matching machine preview. historical_committed, reconciliation_required, every RunStorageError, effect_unknown, current_may_have_advanced, release failure, outcome mismatch, reconstructed/reparsed authorization, or any value not issued by that factory returns no authority.

The orchestrator, not the coordinator and not an arbitrary callback, applies an authorized plan through one state-machine lock and a closed applied/already_applied/apply_failed/apply_unknown result. All validation and injected pre-mutation faults occur before replacing the event list and state and return apply_failed; exact event already present returns already_applied; response loss after mutation is reconciled under the same lock to already_applied when exact, otherwise apply_unknown. Exact concurrent replay creates at most one FINAL_SYNTHESIS-to-COMPLETED event, stale/divergent/forged authorization fails closed, and no rollback is claimed.

Fault injection covers forged request/outcome/binding values, secret/classification mismatch, preflight refusal, lock contention and API failure, metadata/namespace/staging/payload/manifest/revision rename faults, CAS and pointer ambiguity, directory-sync failure, lock-release failure, current/historical replay, idempotency payload conflict, orphan/reconciliation outcome, pre-apply and post-observation apply faults, concurrent writer, and concurrent exact replay. No denied or uncertain storage outcome authorizes COMPLETED.

A published structural revision followed by an in-memory apply failure is reported as apply_failed or apply_unknown without rollback or deletion claims. Recovery is limited to exact request replay plus idempotent apply against a matching live machine; process-restart reconstruction, durable resume, terminal visibility, public completed status, migration, and orphan repair remain P2-012B or later.

Windows directory-sync unavailable may authorize a successfully reconciled published outcome only for the tested local cooperating-process visibility contract. P2-010B makes no power-loss, hardware-cache, cross-volume, UNC, SMB, NFS, distributed, malicious-writer, universal directory-durability, or process-crash state-recovery claim.

Ordinary flat-v1 behavior remains byte/order/signature compatible, including Orchestrator.run/resume/load_report, CLI commands and exit codes, CaseInput, FinalReport, ToolResult, serial phase order, golden normalization, calculation assignment artifacts, and the assigned-but-unexecuted report-writer. The characterized flat-v1 COMPLETED-before-final-report-write fault remains explicitly unresolved and is not represented as fixed by this opt-in seam.

P2-010A phase contracts remain versioned internal APIs and are not exported as stable package-root APIs. Pure phases still do no filesystem, state-machine, provider, tool, network, approval-ledger, ambient-clock, or ambient-random mutation; provider and tool effects remain behind their existing executors, and only the orchestrator may request or apply a transition.

Execution remains serial with zero automatic retries and peak concurrency one. P2-010B does not add durable usage, reservation, multi-process budget CAS, retry scheduling, parallel agents, cancellation fan-out, provider execution, external solver execution, runtime bridges, sandboxing, or approval CAS, and it does not change budget observation or settlement semantics.

P2-010B accepts only poker-final-report-artifact-v2 on a dedicated revision root whose ownership marker exactly matches RunRevisionStore producer_id p2-010b-phase-revision and producer_version 0.2.0. Before the target run's initial publication, inspection must prove that target run has no current pointer or revision history; histories for other run IDs are outside this check. After a published revision exists, only an explicit same-process replay of the original frozen request/plan bundle whose run, transaction, transaction digest, revision, manifest, and pointer exactly produce current_committed is exempt; different transaction, historical, successor, reconstructed, or cross-process replay is denied. Same-canonical-build, no-mixed-build, and no-rolling access are trusted deployment assumptions which the unchanged schemas cannot attest, detect, or prevent, so violation is unsupported rather than claimed to fail closed. Producer mismatch, nonexact target-run history, v1 final report, or old reader fails; new readers retain v1 read support, old readers reject explicit v2, and no cross-build availability, migration, rewrite, or conversion claim is made.

Capabilities, doctor, README, architecture, phase, storage, security, context, budget, tool, limitation, and generated roadmap docs state the narrow internal structural integration and separately approved final-report artifact v2 boundary truthfully. immutable_revision_storage_foundation stays implemented; product_integrated_durable_run stays planned; no GTO, equilibrium, exploitability, exact-range, external-provider, external-solver, parallel, retry, terminal, resume, migration, cleanup, encryption, or secure-erase capability is promoted.

Dedicated-root contract: RunRevisionStore and initialize_revision_root both require explicit revision_root and legacy_runs_root Path parameters, resolve them without mutation, and reject equality or either ancestor/descendant overlap even when both directories are empty. The legacy root must already be a regular non-reparse directory; its canonical platform-normalized resolved path, adapter, st_dev, and st_ino are hashed under poker-run-legacy-root-identity-v1 and only legacy_runs_root_identity_sha256 is persisted in OwnershipMarkerV1. Construction and ordinary read methods are side-effect-free. initialize_revision_root alone accepts a missing or existing empty dedicated directory, pins canonical root identity, and writes OwnershipMarkerV1 plus control directories without artifact input. Every initialization, read, inspect, publish, and recovery operation recomputes and requires the exact persisted legacy root identity before trusting or mutating the revision root. Publish requires that marker and ASCII-case-fold scans both revision_root/runs and the bound legacy_runs_root siblings; wrong/missing ownership or legacy identity, any exact/case-alias flat-v1 marker or artifact for that logical run ID, mixed namespace, or revision sibling alias fails closed without run-namespace mutation. Because unchanged legacy RunStore does not take the revision lock, callers must not concurrently create the same case-folded legacy run ID during revision publication; P2-012A detects deterministic preexisting collisions but does not claim atomic cross-root exclusion against a concurrently started legacy writer.

Portable run identity: reuse the tested RunStore run-ID grammar ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$ and additionally require NFC, one portable segment, no trailing dot/space, no CON/PRN/AUX/NUL/COM1-COM9/LPT1-LPT9 stem including extension aliases, and no ASCII-case alias among revision-root run siblings. The lock key is lowercase SHA-256 over the ASCII-case-folded NFC run ID UTF-8 bytes prefixed by the ASCII domain poker-run-lock-key-v1 followed by one 0x00 byte, so first-use aliases share one authority before the sibling scan.

Foundation versions: use frozen strict StorageRevisionManifestV1 schema 1.0.0, StorageRevisionPointerV1 schema 1.0.0, RevisionTransactionDescriptorV1 schema 1.0.0, lock metadata/recovery claim/failure schema 1.0.0, storage protocol poker-run-revision-v1, canonicalization poker-run-storage-json-v1, and lowercase unkeyed SHA-256. P2-012A writes publication_kind=structural_nonterminal and rejects all terminal, old, future, or unknown versions. P2-012B must introduce and explicitly dispatch separately approved RunManifestV2, CompletionMarkerV2, and terminal pointer schemas; it must not change any A schema field or meaning.

Manifest exact fields: StorageRevisionManifestV1 contains only schema_version, storage_protocol, canonicalization, hash_algorithm, publication_kind, run_id, revision, transaction_id, transaction_sha256, previous_revision, previous_manifest_sha256, expected_pointer_sha256, created_at, producer_id, producer_version, inventory_sha256, provenance_heads, and artifacts. manifest_sha256 is the derived lowercase SHA-256 of exact canonical manifest bytes and is never serialized inside the manifest.

Pointer exact fields: StorageRevisionPointerV1 contains only schema_version, storage_protocol, canonicalization, hash_algorithm, publication_kind, run_id, revision, transaction_id, revision_relative_path, transaction_sha256, manifest_sha256, inventory_sha256, and published_at. pointer_sha256 is derived from exact canonical pointer bytes and is never serialized inside the pointer; revision_relative_path is recomputed from revision and transaction_id and must match.

Transaction exact fields: RevisionTransactionDescriptorV1 contains only schema_version, storage_protocol, canonicalization, hash_algorithm, run_id, transaction_id, proposed_revision, expected_revision, expected_manifest_sha256, expected_pointer_sha256, created_at, producer_id, producer_version, artifact_plan, provenance_heads, and transaction_sha256. The transaction digest is SHA-256 of ASCII poker-run-storage-transaction-v1, one 0x00 byte, and canonical JSON of all preceding descriptor fields except transaction_sha256. created_at is strict timezone-aware UTC supplied once by an injectable clock and frozen in the request/descriptor; owner token, PID, acquired UTC, claim data, temp path, outcome, fault and durability evidence are excluded.

Revision and random identity: the initial revision is integer 1 with null previous revision/manifest/pointer expectations; every successor is exactly current plus one. Transaction, owner, and claim IDs are respectively txn-, owner-, and claim- plus 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits produced by injectable 128-bit generators; tests use deterministic factories and production defaults use secrets.token_hex(16).

Ownership and lock schemas: OwnershipMarkerV1 contains only schema_version=1.0.0, ownership_kind=poker_revision_root, storage_protocol, canonicalization, hash_algorithm, root_id, legacy_runs_root_identity_sha256, initialized_at, producer_id, and producer_version; root_id is root- plus 32 lowercase hex from the injected ID factory and marker_sha256 is the derived lowercase SHA-256 of exact canonical marker bytes, never serialized. legacy_runs_root_identity_sha256 is SHA-256 of ASCII poker-run-legacy-root-identity-v1, one 0x00 byte, and canonical JSON containing only adapter, platform-normalized NFC resolved path, integer st_dev, and integer st_ino; the path itself is never serialized. LockMetadataV1 contains only schema_version=1.0.0, storage_protocol, run_id_sha256, ownership_marker_sha256, authority_identity_sha256, owner_token, process_id, adapter restricted to windows_msvcrt or posix_fcntl, nullable transaction_id, nullable expected_revision, and acquired_at. authority_identity_sha256 is SHA-256 of ASCII poker-run-authority-identity-v1, one 0x00 byte, and canonical JSON containing only adapter, integer st_dev, and integer st_ino read from the opened authority handle; it contains no path. Metadata is advisory and has no self-hash field.

RecoveryClaimV1 exact fields: schema_version=1.0.0, storage_protocol, canonicalization, hash_algorithm, run_id_sha256, transaction_id, transaction_sha256, nullable observed_pointer_sha256, orphan_form restricted to staging or unreferenced_revision, claim_id, claimant_token, claimed_at, and claim_sha256. claim_sha256 is SHA-256 of ASCII poker-run-recovery-claim-v1, one 0x00 byte, and canonical JSON of all preceding fields except claim_sha256.
