Outcome and durability schemas: DurabilityEvidenceV1 contains only schema_version=1.0.0, platform_adapter restricted to windows_msvcrt or posix_fcntl, file_sync restricted to not_attempted, confirmed, or failed, directory_sync restricted to not_attempted, confirmed, unavailable, or failed, pointer_replace restricted to not_attempted, attempted_unconfirmed, or confirmed, and reconciliation restricted to confirmed or required. RevisionPublishOutcomeV1 contains only schema_version=1.0.0, outcome_kind restricted to published, current_committed, historical_committed, or reconciliation_required, run_id_sha256, transaction_id, transaction_sha256, revision, nullable observed_current_revision, nullable manifest_sha256, nullable pointer_sha256, filesystem_effect, domain_effect, previous_revision_effect, and durability_evidence. The exact cross-field matrix is closed: published requires nonnull observed_current_revision equal to revision, nonnull manifest_sha256 and pointer_sha256, filesystem_effect=current_advanced, domain_effect=current_advanced, previous_revision_effect=not_applicable exactly when revision=1 and unchanged exactly when revision>1, file_sync=confirmed, directory_sync=confirmed or unavailable but never failed/not_attempted, pointer_replace=confirmed, and reconciliation=confirmed; current_committed requires nonnull observed_current_revision equal to revision, nonnull manifest_sha256 and pointer_sha256, filesystem_effect=none, domain_effect=current_unchanged, previous_revision_effect=not_applicable exactly when revision=1 and unchanged exactly when revision>1, file_sync=not_attempted, directory_sync=not_attempted, pointer_replace=not_attempted, and reconciliation=confirmed; historical_committed requires nonnull observed_current_revision greater than revision, nonnull manifest_sha256 for the historical revision and pointer_sha256 for the verified observed current, filesystem_effect=none, domain_effect=current_unchanged, previous_revision_effect=not_applicable exactly when revision=1 and unchanged exactly when revision>1, file_sync=not_attempted, directory_sync=not_attempted, pointer_replace=not_attempted, and reconciliation=confirmed; reconciliation_required requires durability reconciliation=required, filesystem_effect restricted to staging_orphan, unreferenced_revision, current_replace_attempted, or current_advanced, domain_effect restricted to current_unchanged, current_may_have_advanced, or current_advanced consistently with the measured effect, previous_revision_effect not_applicable only for revision=1 or otherwise unchanged/unconfirmed, and permits observed_current_revision, manifest_sha256, or pointer_sha256 to be null only when that value could not be strictly verified. Every forbidden cross-field combination, including any successful outcome with failed sync, fails strict schema validation and is covered by contract tests. Outcomes are returned values, never persisted inside immutable revisions.

Request and artifact schemas: RevisionArtifactV1 contains only logical_name, media_type, artifact_schema_version, serialization, exact_bytes, required, classification, classification_source, classification_evidence, policy_sha256, origin_kind, and provenance_bindings; the classification triple must reconstruct the complete strict ArtifactClassification and policy_sha256 must equal the approved P2-027A digest. origin_kind is restricted to case_input, normalization_output, assumption_ledger, evidence_ledger, approval_ledger, assignment_ledger, agent_execution_ledger, security_event_ledger, dispute_ledger, agent_report, tool_input, tool_result, final_report_json, or final_report_markdown and must match the logical-name table. exact_bytes is an in-memory immutable bytes value and source/hash/size/path/classification-evidence-hash fields are derived. RevisionPublishRequestV1 contains only schema_version=1.0.0, run_id, transaction_id, proposed_revision, nullable expected_revision, nullable expected_manifest_sha256, nullable expected_pointer_sha256, created_at, producer_id, producer_version, and artifacts. proposed_revision must be 1 for null expectations or expected_revision plus one; artifacts are normalized to the approved path order before transaction construction.

Root initialization request/outcome schemas: RootInitializationRequestV1 contains only schema_version=1.0.0, revision_root Path, legacy_runs_root Path, root_id, initialized_at, producer_id, and producer_version; paths are in-memory only and never serialized into control files. RootInitializationInspectionV1 contains only schema_version=1.0.0, status restricted to uninitialized, incomplete, initialized, or corrupt, nullable root_id, nullable ownership_marker_sha256, and recognized_relative_paths sorted by UTF-8 bytes. RootInitializationOutcomeV1 contains only schema_version=1.0.0, outcome_kind restricted to initialized, already_initialized, or reconciliation_required, root_id, nullable ownership_marker_sha256, filesystem_effect restricted to none or control_only, and durability_evidence. Its closed matrix is: initialized requires nonnull marker hash, control_only, file_sync=confirmed, directory_sync=confirmed or unavailable but never failed/not_attempted, pointer_replace=not_attempted, reconciliation=confirmed; already_initialized requires nonnull marker hash, none, file_sync/directory_sync/pointer_replace all not_attempted, reconciliation=confirmed; reconciliation_required requires control_only, pointer_replace=not_attempted, reconciliation=required, permits marker hash null only when not strictly verified, and permits file/directory sync states only as measured at the failed boundary. Every other combination fails strict validation.

Inspection schemas: VerifiedStorageRevisionV1 contains only schema_version=1.0.0, verification_kind=structural_nonterminal, run_id, current_revision, current_pointer_sha256, manifest_sha256, inventory_sha256, and reachable_history entries; each reachable entry contains only revision, transaction_id, revision_relative_path, transaction_sha256, and manifest_sha256 ordered current-to-genesis. OrphanInspectionV1 contains only schema_version=1.0.0, run_id_sha256, nullable current_pointer_sha256, reachable_history, staging_orphans, and revision_orphans. Each orphan contains only orphan_form, verification_state restricted to path_only, descriptor_verified, or manifest_verified, transaction_id, nullable transaction_sha256, nullable revision, and relative_path; partial first-revision staging therefore remains representable without inventing current or descriptor hashes. These values are internal, redacted, and do not mean completed, resumable, or terminal.

Artifact-plan and provenance-head schemas: RevisionTransactionDescriptorV1.artifact_plan and StorageRevisionManifestV1.artifacts are the same tuple of complete PayloadInventoryEntryV1 values sorted by revision_relative_path UTF-8 bytes; caller order is discarded before digesting and duplicates/aliases are rejected. ProvenanceHeadV1 contains only kind, binding_count, and bindings_sha256, where bindings_sha256 uses the approved per-kind head domain and ordered binding digests; provenance_heads is a tuple of ProvenanceHeadV1 sorted by kind UTF-8 bytes with one head per present kind and no empty head.

Frozen clock values: initialize_revision_root freezes initialized_at once before its control-byte plan; a publish request freezes created_at once during pure preflight and reuses that exact value for transaction created_at and pointer published_at. Immediately after successful kernel acquisition it freezes acquired_at once, constructs exact metadata bytes, and then performs locked admission before metadata write. A recovery request separately freezes claimed_at before its pure preflight and reuses it on retry. All times are timezone-aware UTC from injected clocks, never regenerated for the same request/descriptor, never used as stale-lock authority, and never included in transaction identity except the explicitly frozen created_at field.

Root initialization protocol and concurrency: after legacy-root identity, nonoverlap, emptiness/recognized-entry, and complete path preflight, initialize_revision_root uses a module-global mutex to reserve a stable intent key of pinned canonical parent identity plus case-folded final root segment before it may create the dedicated root directory. Every caller, including one that sees an existing root, checks and reserves this intent key; after root creation/detection it atomically adds the pinned root-identity alias key to the same reservation without releasing the intent key, and both keys remain held through kernel/registry release. If either key is already reserved, the call returns RunLocked. Release uncertainty conservatively retains the entire alias set. Only then does it create or verify the stable root-level .revision-init.authority.lock one-byte file and acquire one nonblocking kernel lock before any owner-specific temp, using the platform-specific Windows byte-range or POSIX whole-file semantics defined below; the authority file is never replaced, unlinked, or truncated and follows the same zero-length repair rules as run locks. Concurrent initialize or reconcile calls for the same root serialize on this authority: an overlap returns RunLocked with root stage and control_only if this call created/repaired authority, while a later call under the lock returns already_initialized only for the same root_id and legacy identity, run_namespace_conflict for a different root_id/legacy identity, or reconciliation_required for the exact single-root partial descriptor. Under the lock, initialize rechecks the entire root and legacy identity; it then canonical-writes root-level ownership.<root_id>.tmp, flushes/fsyncs/closes/rereads it as the durable recovery descriptor, creates only recognized .revision-control.<root_id>.tmp and runs.<root_id>.tmp directories plus locks inside the control temp, renames both unique directories to .revision-control and runs only if finals are absent, atomically replaces ownership.json from the already-verified ownership temp last, rereads all identities, and attempts supported directory sync. Before the final marker is verified, side-effect-free inspect_root_initialization derives root_id from the verified ownership temp and returns incomplete, and all publish/orphan-inspect operations refuse with root_initialization_incomplete. reconcile_revision_root takes the same root-init authority lock and requires the original RootInitializationRequestV1 root_id, exact legacy root identity, and expected canonical marker SHA-256; it accepts exactly one consistent recognized root ID across final/temp entries and may only finish missing approved renames/marker publication. Different/multiple IDs, unknown entries, invalid/corrupt temp, or hash mismatch fail mutation-zero for manual review, and no partial entry is deleted or silently adopted. Fault and concurrency tests cover two processes behind a preflight barrier plus the same-process transition race where caller A pauses after root mkdir but before authority acquire and caller B begins through an existing-path alias; different root IDs cannot both create owner-specific state.

Canonical bytes: control JSON is UTF-8 without BOM or trailing newline, sorted-key compact JSON with non-ASCII preserved, finite values only, and strings/keys required already NFC rather than silently normalized; duplicate keys including post-NFC aliases are rejected. Every datetime is encoded only as RFC3339 UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ with exactly six fractional digits and literal Z; naive, nonzero-offset, +00:00, or other precision forms are rejected as noncanonical. Payload serialization literals are poker-run-storage-json-v1, poker-run-storage-jsonl-v1, poker-run-storage-utf8-text-v1, and opaque-bytes-v1; JSON/JSONL/text inputs must already be canonical, and opaque bytes are allowed only for an explicitly approved non-JSON logical-name table entry. JSONL is zero or more individually canonical JSON objects, each followed by exactly one LF byte including the final record, with empty file allowed and blank lines, CRLF, BOM, and unterminated final records rejected. UTF-8 text has no BOM, requires NFC and LF-only line endings, permits empty bytes, and preserves caller-supplied presence or absence of one final LF. The writer never deserializes and reserializes accepted payload bytes.

Inventory exact contract: each PayloadInventoryEntryV1 contains logical_name, revision_relative_path, media_type, artifact_schema_version, serialization, size_bytes, sha256, required, classification, classification_source, classification_evidence, classification_evidence_sha256, source_sha256, and provenance_bindings. classification_evidence is the complete strict non-secret ClassificationEvidence object with source_classifications, nullable explicit_classification, explicit_source_trusted, restricted_secret_check_completed, and contains_restricted_secret; classification_evidence_sha256 is derived as SHA-256 of ASCII poker-run-classification-evidence-v1, one 0x00 byte, and its exact canonical JSON. Paths are NFC POSIX relative paths ordered by UTF-8 bytes and reject duplicate physical/logical, case, trailing-dot-space, reserved-device, or NFC aliases. Every listed artifact must exist and verify in P2-012A even when required=false; required is frozen only for future product completeness interpretation.

Inventory digest: inventory_sha256 is SHA-256 of ASCII poker-run-storage-inventory-v1, one 0x00 byte, and canonical JSON of the ordered complete inventory. It is an inventory root, not a Merkle-tree claim. manifest.json, transaction.json, current.json, authority/metadata, all temps, recovery claims, future completion.json, and future quarantine metadata are excluded from payload inventory but included where specified in structural verification and byte accounting.

Logical media/schema admission table: input.json is application/json, poker-run-storage-json-v1, poker-case-input-artifact-v1, and one strict redacted CaseInput object; normalized_case.json is application/json, poker-run-storage-json-v1, poker-normalized-case-artifact-v1, and one strict CaseInput equal to NormalizationOutput.normalized_case; assumptions.json is application/json, poker-run-storage-json-v1, poker-assumption-list-artifact-v1, and an array of strict Assumption; evidence.jsonl is application/x-ndjson, poker-run-storage-jsonl-v1, poker-evidence-record-jsonl-artifact-v1, and zero or more strict EvidenceRecord; approvals.json is application/json, poker-run-storage-json-v1, poker-approval-request-list-artifact-v1, and an array of strict ApprovalRequest; assignments.json is application/json, poker-run-storage-json-v1, poker-agent-assignment-list-artifact-v1, and an array of strict AgentAssignment; agent_execution_records.json is application/json, poker-run-storage-json-v1, poker-agent-execution-record-list-artifact-v1, and an array of strict AgentExecutionRecord; security_events.json is application/json, poker-run-storage-json-v1, poker-security-event-list-artifact-v1, and an array of strict SecurityEvent; disputes.json is application/json, poker-run-storage-json-v1, poker-dispute-list-artifact-v1, and an array of strict Dispute; agent_reports/<portable-id>.json is application/json, poker-run-storage-json-v1, poker-agent-report-artifact-v1, and one strict AgentReport whose report_id matches the path; tool_results/<portable-id>.input.json is application/json, poker-run-storage-json-v1, poker-tool-input-artifact-v1, and the exact canonical object accepted by the bound ToolRequest plus registry contract/version; tool_results/<portable-id>.json is application/json, poker-run-storage-json-v1, poker-tool-result-artifact-v1, and one strict ToolResult whose result_id/path/tool/version/input hashes match ToolBindingV1; final_report.json is application/json, poker-run-storage-json-v1, poker-final-report-artifact-v1, and one strict FinalReport whose run_id matches; final_report.md is text/markdown, poker-run-storage-utf8-text-v1, poker-final-report-markdown-artifact-v1, and exact renderer output bound to the final_report.json hash. Every existing Pydantic-domain validator is invoked through strict=True validation/TypeAdapter; the validated model is then dumped through poker-run-storage-json-v1 and those bytes must equal the exact input bytes byte-for-byte, or each JSONL validated dump plus LF must equal its exact input line plus LF. Any coercion, inserted default/generated ID/time, v1 migration, CaseInput label/confidence normalization, or ToolResult normalization therefore returns artifact_schema_error; these and unknown fields, string-to-number, bool/int, container, and datetime coercions are adversarial cases. state.json, .poker-deliberation-run, every unlisted logical name/media/schema combination, and opaque-bytes-v1 are refused in P2-012A.

Classification admission and replay: RevisionArtifact must contain the complete ArtifactClassification and trusted evidence inputs, typed origin_kind, and declared policy SHA-256. Before lock/filesystem mutation the store reruns classify_artifact(logical_name, every exact ClassificationEvidence field), requires exact classification, classification_source, and P2-027A policy SHA-256 508fe62ce72ae54b59a8d71e200309a2046bf807dcf249f0aebf787c910cab60, refuses ClassificationSource.DEFAULT_INTERNAL, and requires trusted explicit or verified source-inherited public/internal classification with a completed clean restricted-secret check for both. The complete non-secret evidence, source, derived evidence hash, and policy binding are persisted; every structural read/reachable-history/orphan verification strictly reconstructs ArtifactClassification, reruns the same classifier under that exact policy, and requires equality with inventory and LocalDataBindingV1. Attempt context, sensitive, restricted, unknown, downgrade, mismatch, forged evidence hash, or encryption-required data is denied. This replayable provenance is structural verification only and grants no P2-012B lifecycle action.

Context boundary: ContextPolicy and ContextEnvelope stay schema 1.0.0 with poker-context-json-v1 and attempt-memory-only-v1. Raw ContextEnvelope, canonical provider context payload, ContextPolicy, credentials, and blinded upstream provider/agent input are never payload artifacts; only non-secret typed context hashes/lineage may appear in provenance. CaseInput, normalized artifacts, and final synthesis may contain the already-approved full retrospective hand/result information under their existing schemas and blind-isolation flow. Storage does not act as a semantic blind-isolation detector and does not claim to detect every secret or defeat a malicious trusted caller that forges classification evidence.

Typed provenance union: the only binding kind literals are approval_decision, context, phase, budget_policy, tool, local_data, source, and report; every binding has that discriminator and only immutable scalar/tuple kind-specific fields, whose hashes retain their originating framework domains rather than being reinterpreted by storage canonicalization. ApprovalDecisionBindingV1 contains kind, approval_id, decision restricted to approved or rejected, decided_at, decision_reason_sha256, and external_source_id. decision_reason_sha256 is SHA-256 of ASCII poker-approval-decision-reason-v1, one 0x00 byte, and the exact NFC UTF-8 decision_reason. external_source_id is exactly approval-decision- plus approval_id. Its canonical decision evidence projection contains only approval_id, status, decision_reason, and decided_at in the approved storage UTC form; source_sha256 is SHA-256 of ASCII poker-approval-decision-evidence-v1, one 0x00 byte, and canonical JSON of that projection. The binding records correlation only and does not validate actor identity, authority, or decision CAS, which remain P2-013. ContextBindingV1 contains kind, context_sha256, context_id, attempt_id, nullable parent_context_id, schema_version, classification, payload_sha256, source_sha256, policy_sha256, envelope_sha256, expires_at UTC, producer_runtime, and consumer_runtime and cross-checks every corresponding AgentExecutionRecord field. PhaseBindingV1 contains kind, run_id, phase_id, phase_schema_version, attempt_id, ordered unique context_ids, input_hash, policy_snapshot_hash, nullable output_hash, and the exact ordered ArtifactIntent tuple of kind, relative_path, media_type, and nullable content_sha256 from the bound PhaseOutcome. Every tuple field/null is preserved and cross-checked; the current synthesis state.json intent remains in PhaseBinding evidence but is excluded from P2-012A payload admission, intents grant no write authority, and each admitted intent with nonnull content_sha256 must match its inventory entry. BudgetPolicyBindingV1 contains kind, policy_schema_version fixed to the exact BudgetPolicyV2.schema_version value, and policy_sha256 only; no nonexistent policy_version field is invented. ToolBindingV1 contains kind, run_id, phase_attempt_id, ordinal, request_id, request_tool_name, requested_by, requires_approval, nullable requested_contract_version, tool_request_sha256, request_input_artifact_sha256, result_id, result_tool_name, result_artifact_sha256, request_input_sha256, validated_result_input_sha256, materialized_result_input_sha256, supported_contract_version, and result_contract_version. Every copied nonnull version string, including phase_schema_version, context schema_version, report_schema_version, and tool contract versions, must match ^[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z._+-]{0,63}$ and its originating typed value exactly. tool_request_sha256 is phases.contracts.canonical_sha256 over the complete ToolRequest request_id/tool_name/input/requested_by/requires_approval/contract_version projection; preflight reconstructs and strictly revalidates that complete request from immutable fields plus the paired input artifact, revalidates the exact result artifact, and enforces every current ToolExecutionBinding correlation. LocalDataBindingV1 contains kind, policy_id, policy_version, policy_sha256, logical_name, classification, classification_source, complete classification_evidence, and derived classification_evidence_sha256; every artifact has exactly one and it must equal every corresponding RevisionArtifactV1 and inventory field. SourceBindingV1 contains kind, source_id, source_kind restricted to user_input, payload_artifact, or external_evidence, trust_kind restricted respectively to trusted_user_input, verified_payload, or declared_external_evidence, nullable source_logical_name, nullable source_schema_version, nullable consumer_record_id, and source_sha256. user_input/external_evidence require null source_schema_version; payload_artifact requires exact equality with the referenced inventory artifact_schema_version. ReportBindingV1 contains kind, report_id, report_schema_version, report_json_sha256, rendered_markdown_sha256, and upstream_source_sha256; for final_report.md, report_id equals FinalReport.run_id, report_schema_version equals final_report.json artifact_schema_version, report_json_sha256 equals that inventory payload hash, rendered_markdown_sha256 equals the markdown payload hash, and upstream_source_sha256 equals final_report.json inventory source_sha256.

Immutable snapshot boundary: RevisionArtifactV1 construction immediately deep model-dumps and revalidates any existing domain model, classification evidence, and provenance input, canonicalizes them into owned immutable bytes plus scalar/tuple storage bindings, and discards all caller-owned dict/list/model references. RevisionPublishRequestV1 likewise owns a tuple of those snapshots; pure preflight and locked publication read only owned bytes/snapshots and never reread caller objects. Caller-owned mutable inputs must not be mutated from constructor entry until snapshot success; detected structural mutation is rejected, but undetectable concurrent same-shape value mutation during construction is outside the supported threat model. After successful snapshot creation, any original-object mutation before or during publish cannot change transaction, inventory, manifest, or stored bytes and is covered by adversarial tests.

Provenance order and digest: binding_sha256 is a derived nonserialized value equal to SHA-256 of ASCII poker-run-provenance-binding-v1, one 0x00 byte, and the complete canonical binding JSON, so no binding self-reference exists. The total order is the typed tuple of kind UTF-8 bytes followed by the kind-specific primary identity: approval request ID, context_id/attempt_id, run_id/phase_id/attempt_id, budget policy SHA-256, run_id/phase_attempt_id/ordinal as a nonnegative integer/result_id, policy ID/logical_name, source ID, or report ID; canonical binding bytes break any remaining tie. Exact duplicate binding digests and duplicate primary identity with different bytes are rejected. Manifest provenance_heads are ordered by kind UTF-8 bytes and each head is SHA-256 of ASCII poker-run-provenance-head-v1, one 0x00 byte, kind UTF-8, one 0x00 byte, and canonical JSON of that kind's ordered binding digests.

Provenance correlation and exact source graph: every artifact has exactly one LocalDataBindingV1. Its policy_id is exactly p2-027a-local-data-policy-v1, policy_version exactly 1.0.0, and policy_sha256 equals RevisionArtifactV1.policy_sha256 and the fixed approved digest; its logical name, classification, classification source/evidence/hash exactly equal the RevisionArtifact and inventory fields, while inventory deliberately does not duplicate policy fields. Every payload_artifact SourceBinding must name an earlier artifact in the approved current-orchestrator dependency order and must exactly match that same-revision inventory entry's logical_name, artifact_schema_version, and payload SHA-256; source_id is payload- plus SHA-256 of ASCII poker-payload-source-id-v1, one 0x00 byte, and source logical-name UTF-8; trust_kind=verified_payload and consumer_record_id=null. Self, future, circular, cross-run, duplicate, conflicting, or unlisted payload edges fail closed. input.json has exactly one user_input SourceBinding with source_id=user-input, trust_kind=trusted_user_input, null logical/schema/consumer fields, and source_sha256 equal to SHA-256 of ASCII poker-user-input-source-v1, one 0x00 byte, and exact input payload bytes. normalized_case.json, assumptions.json, and security_events.json each bind input.json. approvals.json binds input.json; every pending ApprovalRequest has no ApprovalDecisionBinding, while every approved/rejected request requires exactly one matching ApprovalDecisionBindingV1 and exactly one external_evidence SourceBinding with source_id equal to external_source_id, trust_kind=declared_external_evidence, null logical/schema/consumer fields, and source_sha256 equal to the canonical decision-evidence hash; status, nonnull reason/decided_at, reason hash, and evidence projection must match the strict ApprovalRequest. Storage does not claim actor authority or approval CAS. evidence.jsonl has one external_evidence SourceBinding per strict EvidenceRecord: source_id and consumer_record_id both equal evidence_id, trust_kind=declared_external_evidence, logical/schema null, and source_sha256 is SHA-256 of ASCII poker-evidence-record-source-v1, one 0x00 byte, and canonical JSON of that complete record; it also has one file-level payload binding to input.json. assignments.json binds normalized_case.json. agent_execution_records.json binds assignments.json and normalized_case.json plus matching ContextBindingV1 and PhaseBindingV1. Each agent_reports/*.json binds assignments.json and normalized_case.json plus matching ContextBindingV1 and PhaseBindingV1; if the ordered unique union of AgentReport.evidence_ids and every nested Claim.evidence_ids is nonempty it also binds evidence.jsonl exactly once and every declared ID must resolve to a strict record in that file, and it binds each distinct earlier tool_results/<id>.json named by the ordered unique AgentReport.tool_result_ids. Duplicate, unknown, cross-run, or future evidence/tool IDs fail closed; the later aggregate execution ledger is correlation evidence, not a report data source. Each tool_results/*.input.json binds input.json and normalized_case.json, never assignments.json, plus matching PhaseBindingV1 and ToolBindingV1; its paired tool_results/*.json binds exactly that input artifact plus matching PhaseBindingV1 and ToolBindingV1. disputes.json binds every present agent report and tool-result JSON, never tool-input alone. final_report.json binds input.json, normalized_case.json, assumptions.json, evidence.jsonl exactly once, approvals.json, assignments.json, agent_execution_records.json, security_events.json, every agent report, every tool input/result pair, and disputes.json plus declared context/phase heads and BudgetPolicyBindingV1. Its embedded evidence, approvals, agent_execution_records, security_events, tool_results, and disputes arrays must equal the corresponding parsed ledger payloads exactly in order and content. final_report.md has exactly one payload_artifact SourceBinding naming final_report.json and exactly one fully correlated ReportBindingV1. source_sha256 is SHA-256 of ASCII poker-run-upstream-bindings-v1, one 0x00 byte, and canonical JSON of direct SourceBindingV1 values sorted first by the typed logical-name key (0, empty bytes) for null or (1, source_logical_name UTF-8) otherwise, then source_id UTF-8, then by (0, empty bytes) for null consumer_record_id or (1, consumer_record_id UTF-8) otherwise; null therefore sorts before nonnull without coercion. Property tests permute user_input, external_evidence, and payload_artifact bindings including null/non-null fields and reject every trust mismatch, record mismatch, duplicate, and future-edge permutation.

Control metadata safety: producer_id and producer_version are injected trusted application constants, not caller free text. Every caller-originated control/provenance identifier uses its existing strict typed ID or the tested portable grammar with the existing 128-character bound; versions use a fixed approved literal or the existing bounded contract-version field. All control strings require NFC, reject path/URI/control characters and Windows reserved aliases where path-like, and pass the P2-027A secret-metadata detector before serialization; raw absolute paths, arbitrary messages, credentials, payload excerpts, and unbounded free text are forbidden in manifests, transactions, pointers, lock metadata, recovery claims, outcomes, and provenance.

Layout: root-init authority=<revision_root>/.revision-init.authority.lock; ownership marker=<revision_root>/ownership.json and temp=<revision_root>/ownership.<root_id>.tmp; initialization directory temps=<revision_root>/.revision-control.<root_id>.tmp and <revision_root>/runs.<root_id>.tmp; run authority=<revision_root>/.revision-control/locks/<run_id_sha256>.authority.lock; metadata=<revision_root>/.revision-control/locks/<run_id_sha256>.metadata.json; metadata temp=<revision_root>/.revision-control/locks/<run_id_sha256>.<owner_token>.metadata.tmp; namespace parents=<revision_root>/runs/<run_id>/.revision-store plus transactions, revisions, recovery-claims, and recovery-claims/.tmp; current=<revision_root>/runs/<run_id>/.revision-store/current.json; pointer temp=<revision_root>/runs/<run_id>/.revision-store/current.<transaction_id>.tmp; staging=<revision_root>/runs/<run_id>/.revision-store/transactions/<transaction_id>/ containing transaction.json, payload/<logical_name>, and manifest.json; immutable revision=<revision_root>/runs/<run_id>/.revision-store/revisions/r<revision>-<transaction_id>/ containing the same transaction.json, payload, and manifest; claim temp=<revision_root>/runs/<run_id>/.revision-store/recovery-claims/.tmp/<transaction_id>.<claim_id>.json; claim final=<revision_root>/runs/<run_id>/.revision-store/recovery-claims/<transaction_id>.json.

Preflight and quota order: pure preflight performs all request/schema/path/classification/media/canonical/provenance checks, exact payload/control sizes, per-artifact limits, and proposed-byte planning before any filesystem mutation. Authority bootstrap/acquisition may then create or repair only the fixed control byte. Under the lock, a mandatory existing-namespace scan first validates bound legacy identity, root/run identity, known entry grammar, regular/link/reparse rules, current/reachable lineage, and current physical total against max_run_bytes; unknown/link/over-cap state fails closed even for replay. Idempotency/current/CAS is then evaluated, and a valid idempotent or conflicting request returns without metadata or namespace write. A genuinely new publish next admits its exact coexistence peak before metadata, namespace bootstrap, staging, claim, or current mutation. Equality is allowed; one byte over fails. A first-use quota/CAS/idempotency refusal can report filesystem_effect=control_only from authority bootstrap but always reports current unchanged.

Byte limits: reuse tested defaults max_artifact_bytes=1000000 and max_run_bytes=10000000; accept only strict positive integers and reject bool/coercion/nonpositive overrides. Per-artifact applies to each payload and canonical control file. Per-run includes current plus temp coexistence, all reachable revisions, staging, unreferenced revisions, claim final/temp files, metadata final/temp, and the attributable one-byte run authority file. Empty approved namespace directories consume no counted file bytes but remain structurally verified. Unknown, link/reparse, hardlinked, or non-regular entries fail closed. Filesystem allocation units, compression, snapshots, root-global ownership/root-init-authority bytes, and flat-v1 files are outside the claim.

Publish order: preflight; process-local nonblocking lock; stable one-byte kernel lock; mandatory locked existing-namespace/identity/link/known-entry/current-lineage/current-byte-cap scan; idempotency and current/CAS read with early return for replay/conflict; exact coexistence-peak admission for a new publish; advisory metadata replace; explicit namespace bootstrap creating each approved run/.revision-store/transactions/revisions/recovery-claims/.tmp parent one level at a time with identity reread; unique staging and transaction descriptor; each payload exclusive write/flush/close/reread/verify; manifest write/flush/close/reread/full inventory verify; same-filesystem staging-to-revision rename; immutable revision plus verified-lineage reread; pointer-temp write/flush/close/reread; root/legacy identity and expected-current recheck; atomic current replace; current/manifest/inventory/lineage reconciliation; supported directory-sync attempts; lock release. CAS and idempotency: compare expected_revision, expected_manifest_sha256, and expected_pointer_sha256 under the lock both before staging and before replace. Same transaction plus same transaction digest at current returns current_committed; if present in verified reachable history returns historical_committed with observed current; if only staging or unreachable revision exists returns reconciliation_required; same transaction plus different digest is idempotency_conflict; stale expected state after lock acquisition is run_conflict. No case silently republishes, advances current, or chooses highest revision.

Reachability: the structural reader starts at a strictly verified current pointer and follows each manifest previous_revision and previous_manifest_sha256 to revision 1/null while enforcing exact decrement, run identity, unique transaction/revision path, transaction descriptor digest, full inventory, and immutable byte hashes. reachable_history is that complete verified chain. Missing/tampered/cyclic/cross-run lineage is corrupt; no partial chain is called verified. Only staging or published revisions outside reachable_history are orphans.

Lock contract: an in-process nonreentrant registry keyed by pinned canonical root identity plus ownership-marker SHA-256 plus ASCII-case-folded run ID prevents same-process instances/threads and root aliases from bypassing process-scoped OS locks. Registry reserve is the first lock action, kernel acquire follows, and release occurs in finally after kernel release attempt; a release fault keeps the registry entry conservatively held for that store process and returns effect_unknown rather than allowing reentry. The stable authority file contains exactly one constant byte; bootstrap or zero-length crash repair writes that byte in place, verifies identity/hardlink count, and never replaces, unlinks, or truncates it. The Windows adapter uses binary mode, seek(0), and msvcrt LK_NBLCK for exactly byte range offset 0 length 1; the POSIX adapter uses fcntl.flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB on the whole authority file and makes no byte-range claim. Metadata is advisory last-owner data, never authority, is atomically replaced under lock, and is not deleted at release. Every acquisition uses its fresh owner_token in the exclusive metadata-temp path; a partial prior temp is a recognized quota-counted control orphan that never blocks a later acquisition's fresh temp, and corrupt/stale final metadata may be replaced only after lock acquisition.

Platform interpretation of the immutable milestone lock criterion: the canonical acceptance text about a one-byte file locked at offset zero for length one is implemented literally by the Windows msvcrt adapter. On POSIX, flock has whole-file semantics; because the verified authority file contains exactly one byte, the whole-file lock excludes all access to that one-byte authority but is not represented or claimed as a POSIX byte-range lock. Platform-specific tests assert these distinct APIs without changing the immutable milestone text.

Wait/stale/retry policy: acquisition makes one nonblocking attempt with no timeout, bounded wait, lease, heartbeat, monotonic stale threshold, cancellation, lock stealing, or automatic retry. PID and UTC are audit-only. RunLocked has retryable=true but automatic_retry_allowed=false; filesystem_effect is none if this call did not bootstrap/repair and control_only if it did before losing the kernel race, while domain/current remain unchanged. All other failures have retryable=false. An overlap returns RunLocked; a separately invoked writer after winner release may acquire and then return RunConflict for stale expected state.

Read and inspect mutation rule: ordinary current/revision structural reads never acquire or create a lock and use pointer-read, full verify, pointer-reread consistency. inspect_orphans requires an already-existing valid one-byte authority and acquires process/kernel locks without creating/repairing authority or writing metadata; missing, zero-length, corrupt, linked, or identity-mismatched authority returns lock_unavailable with mutation zero. Recovery claim is a separate mutating operation and may update metadata/claim files under its locked admission.

Recovery claim: inspect and claim require the authoritative lock and verify the target is staging or an unreferenced published revision outside reachable_history. Only descriptor_verified or manifest_verified targets with a verified transaction_sha256 are claimable; path_only/partial staging is reported by inspection but claim returns run_incomplete with mutation zero. Claim binds transaction ID/digest, observed pointer SHA-256, orphan form, request-stable claimant token, and strict injected UTC. A claim-specific temp is exclusive-created, canonical-written, flushed, reread, and atomically finalized under lock only after final absence and reachability recheck; existing exact valid claim is idempotent across a new process/new lock owner, different valid is recovery_claim_conflict, invalid final is recovery_claim_incomplete with reconciliation required, and partial temp is a recognized quota-counted orphan. Finalize-success followed by result/reconcile fault and a new-process retry of the same request must return the exact idempotent claim. Claim alone grants no publish/approval authority and performs no move/delete/repair/quarantine/adoption.

Path/threat contract: resolve and pin the dedicated root, reject root or descendant symlink/junction/reparse using Python-3.11-compatible lstat and Windows FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT checks, require regular files with link count one, exclusive-create mutable temps, and recheck canonical identity at every deterministic write/publish/CAS boundary. Logical paths reject empty/dot/dot-dot, absolute, drive-relative/absolute, UNC, device, URI, slash mismatch, backslash, colon/ADS, reserved stem, trailing dot/space, NFC alias, and ASCII-case alias. Detected effects reflect the stage; complete syscall-between malicious same-privilege TOCTOU, authenticity, ACL hardening, and native-handle sandboxing are not claimed.

Path-length capability: each operation's pure preflight constructs every concrete path it can use before that operation's first mutation. Root initialization preflights the root itself, .revision-init.authority.lock, ownership.json, ownership.<root_id>.tmp, .revision-control.<root_id>.tmp, runs.<root_id>.tmp, final .revision-control, final runs, and temp/final locks paths; publication/recovery preflights every concrete run authority, metadata final/temp, each namespace parent, staging, transaction, payload, manifest, revision, pointer final/temp, and recovery-claim final/temp path. The Windows msvcrt adapter is conservative legacy-path-only: each resolved absolute path plus its terminating NUL must be at most 260 UTF-16 code units and each segment plus NUL must be at most 256 UTF-16 code units; longer paths return path_confinement_failed with mutation zero, and Windows extended-length paths remain unverified/unimplemented. POSIX checks available PC_PATH_MAX and PC_NAME_MAX from os.pathconf and fails lock_unavailable/path_confinement_failed when the platform cannot establish a supported bound. Boundary tests cover equality, one unit over, every root-initialization and namespace-parent path class, deep revision roots, and long Unicode segments; a late OS path error is never promoted to success and reports the stage-appropriate effect.

items.title: Local data lifecycle
items.objective: Define a versioned local-data classification, retention, expiry, quarantine, disposition, encryption, failure, and audit contract in P2-027A, then add authorized filesystem enforcement only in separately approved P2-027B.
acceptance_criteria: P2-027A provides a strict versioned immutable policy and pure evaluation contract with approved classification mapping, exact retention and expiry semantics, quarantine and disposition candidates, encryption requirements, typed non-retryable failures, canonical hashes, and bounded audit metadata without filesystem mutation.

P2-027A preserves ContextPolicy and ContextEnvelope 1.0.0, attempt-memory-only-v1, existing provider/orchestrator/storage/CLI behavior, blind isolation, tool contracts, exactness, and evidence provenance.

P2-027B remains separately approval-gated after P2-012B and P2-013A and requires verified ownership, active/pending protection, actor authority, approved dry-run action digest, revision CAS, receipts/tombstones, idempotency, and partial-failure reconciliation without claiming secure erase absent platform evidence.
tests: future P2-027B cleanup authorization and reconciliation tests

topics: Implement RM-027 milestone P2-027A only and freeze the full RM-027 contract with P2-027A policy/schema separated from P2-027B filesystem enforcement.
Use strict frozen extra-forbid local-data policy schema 1.0.0, canonicalization poker-local-data-policy-json-v1, and unkeyed SHA-256 without claiming writer authenticity.

Reuse public, internal, sensitive, and restricted classification; default to internal, force detected credentials to restricted, inherit the maximum source classification, forbid automatic downgrade, and never use redaction as downgrade authority.

Require typed application ownership and logical subject kinds; exclude user_materials, goal tmp, review/test output, unowned pytest sessions, Git-tracked source/docs, and paths inferred only from ignores, globs, names, or mtime.
Map current run payload, audit, and report logical artifacts exactly as proposed; unknown logical artifacts fail closed and current v1 artifacts remain legacy_unverified.

Use fixed 24-hour UTC retention days: public run 365, internal run 90, sensitive run 30, restricted 0 with persistence forbidden; cap application cache at 7 and application temp at 1; retain bounded lifecycle audit and disposition metadata for 365; use a 30-day quarantine review window.

Anchor run retention only at a future verified terminal publication, cache/temp at typed application creation, lifecycle audit/receipt at decision commit, and quarantine at quarantine entry; never use filesystem mtime.

Keep ContextPolicy.expires_at as provider use-expiry and separate retention_started_at/retention_expires_at for storage; now at or after expiry creates candidate eligibility only and never executes deletion.

Use disposition values deny_persistence, retain, protected, manual_review, quarantine_candidate, and delete_candidate with active/pending/hold/ownership/integrity/lineage protection taking precedence over destructive eligibility.

Treat incomplete, corrupt, orphan, supported-schema integrity/lineage mismatch, path-confinement failure, and discovered encryption mismatch as quarantine candidates; treat unsupported future versions, legacy v1, unknown policy/classification, unverified ownership, and clock rollback as protected manual review.

Defer encryption implementation and make no at-rest claim for public/internal; require encryption before sensitive persistence and deny it when unavailable; forbid restricted persistence; label current v1 encryption state unknown or unencrypted.
Define the proposed typed non-retryable lifecycle failure taxonomy and require every failure to return no action with filesystem/domain mutation zero.
Define bounded lifecycle audit metadata and pure policy evaluation only; do not persist an audit ledger, receipt, tombstone, raw content, or secret in P2-027A.
Expose local_data_lifecycle_policy as implemented only after acceptance tests pass and local_data_cleanup_executor as unavailable.
Preserve ContextPolicy/ContextEnvelope 1.0.0, attempt-memory-only-v1, existing provider/orchestrator/RunStore/CLI behavior, blind isolation, tool contracts, exactness, and evidence provenance.

Do not implement filesystem discovery, read, write, scan, move, rename, quarantine, delete, cleanup CLI, secure erase, encryption/key management, manifest/CAS, approval actor, receipt/tombstone materialization, P2-012A, RM-013, P2-027B, RM-029 through RM-031, external provider/solver, retry, or parallel execution.
